title.en: Apical four chamber right ventricle focused

idea.en: Shift the four chamber to centre the right heart.

note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of right ventricle

steps.en: What you see: The right ventricle dominates with its crescent wrapped around the septum, the tricuspid annulus wide on screen and the right atrium below. The left ventricle sits at the edge, partly cut off.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values: Tricuspid annular plane excursion 17 mm or more is normal.
Right ventricular basal diameter 42 mm or less is normal.
Right ventricular fractional area change 35 percent or more is normal.

Pitfalls: TAPSE falls after cardiac surgery even when the ventricle is fine, so read it with free wall motion. A septum flattened in systole means pressure overload and in diastole volume overload; timing decides.
Indian context: Long standing rheumatic mitral stenosis raises pulmonary pressure, so this focused right heart view belongs in the follow up of every Indian patient with severe mitral stenosis.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of right ventricle

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Cavity of right ventricle
Anterior papillary muscle of right ventricle

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Left ventricle centred so the right ventricle is cut off. Correct it by sliding medially and angling laterally until the right free wall stands clear of the sector edge.
Apex off screen from too much medial tilt. Correct it by easing back until the apex returns and then rechecking the free wall.
Tricuspid annulus missed by a too lateral plane. Correct it by angling medially a touch until the full annulus and hinge points show.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at apex, fifth intercostal space, slid medial with lateral tilt.
Point the probe marker toward the left, about three o clock.
From the four chamber, slide medially and tilt laterally so the right ventricle fills the screen. Keep the apex on screen so size stays honest.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Spot a pressure loaded D shaped septum.

q.en: TAPSE is 14 mm with good free wall motion after bypass surgery. What next?

o.en: Read with caution since TAPSE falls after surgery

why.en: Postoperative TAPSE understates function, so wall motion decides.

q.en: Basal right ventricular diameter is 48 mm. What does this mean?

why.en: Above 42 mm the right ventricle is dilated by definition.

q.en: Septum flattens in systole only. What load is this?

why.en: Systolic flattening means pressure overload; diastolic flattening means volume.
